identity.name: Propane-1,2-diol alginate (propylene glycol alginate)
synonyms: Propylene glycol ester of alginic acid
identity.chemical_class: Partially esterified alginic acid derivative (alginic acid propylene glycol ester)

function.mechanism: A partially esterified alginate polymer that increases viscosity and helps stabilize oil-water interfaces; the amphiphilic structure supports thickening and emulsion stability.

adi.basis: EFSA (2018) reaffirmed ADI of 55 mg/kg bw/day, based on SCF rationale using a NOAEL of 2,500 mg/kg bw/day from a 2-year rat study and uncertainty factor 45.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported uses/use levels, while noting potential ADI exceedance in conservative toddler and supplement-user scenarios.

fda.notes: Regulated as a food additive with category-specific maximum use levels; not listed as a dedicated GRAS-affirmed monograph in Parts 182/184/186 in the current Title 21 XML reviewed.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry reports ADI range 0-70 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: A 2023 study reported allergy-related mechanisms for propylene glycol alginate sodium sulfate (PSS), including IgE-linked mast-cell signaling; relevance to standard food-grade E405 is indirect.
Recent PubMed literature on propylene glycol alginate is dominated by formulation/materials applications rather than direct chronic oral dietary safety studies in humans.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation concluded no safety concern for the reported uses and use levels.
US CFR permits use under specified concentration limits across food categories.

populations: Consumers of food supplements containing E405 at maximum reported levels
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA identified potential exceedance in conservative scenarios, despite an overall no-safety-concern conclusion at reported uses/use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: E405 remains authorized by EFSA and FDA with explicit ADIs/use limits, and EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported use levels. Potential exceedance appears scenario-dependent (mainly conservative toddler/supplement scenarios), and recent direct oral safety evidence is limited rather than strongly adverse.
key_factors: EFSA ADI 55 mg/kg bw/day with 2018 no-safety-concern conclusion
JECFA ADI range 0-70 mg/kg bw and 1993 evaluation listing
FDA approval under 21 CFR 172.858 with category-specific limits
No IARC classification identified for this additive
Potential ADI exceedance in conservative toddler/supplement scenarios
